subject: ventures/greenhouse-bench-planner
professional: a commercial bedding-plant / transplant grower who plans spring bench space (or a greenhouse production consultant); first checks: are sow dates counted back correctly from sale dates, is bench occupancy summed per week so the peak week is right, is capacity never exceeded, is seeding inflated for germination/survival losses, are hold-early and sell-late trade-offs priced sensibly, and does the space model handle plug-tray sizes and pot-tight vs spaced stages

evidence.correctness: Ran analyze(DEFAULT_CROPS) (node -e import calc.mjs). Hand/date(1) recomputation: Tomato sale 2027-05-08 minus (2+6) wk = 2027-03-13 (date -u -d '2027-05-08 - 56 days'), sown ceil(300/0.92)=327, bench 300/2.2=136.36 sq ft, germ 327/60=5.45 sq ft, margin 300x(3.50-1.10)=$720: all match. Geranium sow 2027-01-30 (date -u -d '2027-05-01 - 91 days') matches. Basil 1 wk late: 240x2.20=528 less 10%x1wk = $475.20 matches; Zinnia 2 wk late: 400x2.60=1040 less 20% = $832 matches. Independent model in scipy HiGHS MILP (scratchpad opt.py, written by the auditor from the page's stated model, not from calc.mjs): unconstrained on-time peak bench 633.106 sq ft (tool 633.106, warning says 634); exact optimum of the same model $4,548.10 / 1,723 units with the same shift choices the tool picks (tool $4,548.10 / 1,723). 25 seeded random instances at 250 sq ft (opt2.py): tool within 0.00-0.39% of the MILP optimum on all, never above it, and 0 weeks over bench or germination capacity. Held below 4 by an input-handling defect: an unquoted '1,200' units field silently shifts every later column and plans a 1-unit crop sown 2023-06-24 at 2.2% survival with no error.
evidence.completeness: README/llms/page features checked end to end: back-scheduled sow dates (works), week-by-week germination and bench table (works, 17 weeks Jan 25-May 17 on the example), hold early / slip late within limits (works: basil +1, zinnia +2), shortfall by crop (works: pepper 63 of 200, basil 240 of 250), margin per sq ft-week ranking (economics table, rendered index.html:171), extra-space sweep +50..+400 (works, monotone in margin), plan CSV (formula-injection guarded) and sowing list (work), 'today' passed-sow-date warning (works: geranium sells 2027-05-31 at earliest = 03-01 + 13 wk), 52-week caps with warnings. README test command `node --test 'ventures/greenhouse-bench-planner/**/*.test.mjs'` from repo root: 33/33 pass. No stubs or TODOs. Not built (stated): saved seasons, multi-house.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject: 33 tests, 33 pass, 0.6 s. Six hand-seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: bench window end (calc.mjs:96) caught, late penalty per week (calc.mjs:102) caught, sown rounding ceil->round (calc.mjs:108) caught, hold penalty times weeks (calc.mjs:102) caught, local-search improvement disabled (calc.mjs:166) caught, survival factor dropped from the germination-capacity bound (calc.mjs:100) SURVIVED: the only germination-limit test uses 100% survival.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (254 lines, pure functions), index.html script (lines 140-192), usage.mjs, all three test files. Clean separation, all user strings escaped (esc) before innerHTML, CSV injection guard, input caps documented with reasons, comma-thousands handled in the option fields (index.html:148). Defects: CSV row parser accepts extra columns silently (calc.mjs:54-61); germSqft reported for germ=0 crops although no germination space is booked (calc.mjs:117); very dense one-line expressions (calc.mjs:59-61, 100-106) that a reviewer would ask to unpack. Acceptable to a senior JS reviewer.
evidence.claims: Checked: '$4,548 against $3,802 for the plain pass' (calc.mjs:135, index.html:110) - plain planCore on the example $3,801.60, rounds to $3,802: backed; 'best plan any of the 5,040 booking orders gives' - enumerated all 5,040 permutations through a copy of planCore with export added: best $4,548.10: backed; llms.txt '1,723 of 1,870 units': backed; 'never reports a bigger bench doing worse' (sweep margin 4548, 4801, 4924, 5091, 5146): backed; privacy/no-network: page.test greps and index imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs: backed; disclaimer 'No warranty ... not legal, tax, accounting, compliance, agronomic, or financial advice' index.html:131 and README/llms: present; usage tracking local-only with four named events, DNT/GPC and opt-out: present and tested. Served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs greenhouse-bench-planner): no placeholder or retired origin. Minor: the sweep is described as what extra space 'would recover', yet 'units short' rises from 37 at +50 to 74 at +100 with no explanation (margin-maximising).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a small spring grower: pasted 7 crops, got sow dates, a weekly bench table with the peak week (2027-03-22 at 400/400), which orders are short, which slip, a CSV and a sowing list, and what +200 sq ft would earn (+$543). A small grower could plan a season with it today. Gaps a commercial user hits: one germination density for all crops (288 vs 72 plug trays), one bench density for the whole crop (no pot-tight then spaced stage), no saved seasons or multiple houses (stated as unbuilt).
evidence.domain: Compared against standard bedding-plant scheduling practice (count back from ship week by crop time; space-cost per sq ft-week as in greenhouse cost accounting; spacing stages pot-tight -> final spacing; plug sizes per crop). The space-week objective, holding cost per sq ft-week and survival-inflated seeding are the right concepts, and the optimiser is near-exact for its model. Departures a senior grower would flag in the first hour: germination density is a single global value (calc.mjs:79) though plug cell counts differ 2-4x by crop; bench density is one value across all growing weeks, so a crop held pot-tight then spaced is over- or under-counted; all losses are taken at seeding, none on the bench; whole-week buckets free the bench for the entire sale week. Limits partly stated ('pot or flat sizes beyond the density you give'), so 2 rather than 1.

defects.what: A crop line with extra fields (e.g. units typed as an unquoted '1,200') is accepted silently: every later column shifts, giving a 1-unit crop with 200 germination weeks, 2.2% survival and a 2023 sow date, with no error. A column-count check would reject it.

Germination density is one global value for every crop, though plug cell counts per sq ft differ 2-4x between crops (e.g. 288 vs 72 trays); germination space and the germination limit are off for mixed lists.
Bench density is one value over all growing weeks: no pot-tight then spaced stage, so the peak-week bench need is wrong for crops spaced partway through (standard bedding-plant practice).
Survival is applied only at seeding; bench space is reserved only for units sold, so bench losses (culls after transplant) never occupy space.

The survival factor in the germination-capacity bound is untested: dropping it leaves all 33 tests green (the only germination-limit test uses 100% survival); with it gone the plan would oversow germination space.
A crop with 0 germination weeks (cuttings stuck straight on the bench) still reports germination sq ft (1.67 for 100 units) in the table and CSV although none is booked.

The extra-space table is framed as what more bench 'would recover' but units short rise from 37 at +50 to 74 at +100 on the example (margin still rises); the page does not say the plan maximises margin, not units.
Weekly buckets free the bench for the whole sale week, so a crop sold Saturday and one benched Monday of the same week are treated as not overlapping.

verdict: Meets the bar for what it claims. The calculator part is unusually strong: every hand-recomputed date, seed count, space figure and penalty matches. An independent MILP of the same model finds exactly the tool's $4,548.10 / 1,723-unit plan on the example. Across 25 random crop lists the tool stays within 0.4% of the optimum and never goes over capacity. The headline claims ($3,802 plain pass, best of 5,040 orders) both reproduce. Five of six seeded mutants are caught. What a commercial grower would hit first is the model, not the maths: one germination density for every crop, one bench density with no spacing stage, and losses only at seeding, so domain is 2. The worst defect is silent column shifting when a number is typed with a thousands comma: the user gets a nonsense plan and no error.
